chain.label: Race eligibility rules exempted modified warbirds from engineering evaluation and flight demonstration
chain.trigger: because the accident airplane was a modified version of a previously designed and built fighter airplane, it was not subject to the more rigorous flight test and analysis that was required to be performed on custom-built airplanes

chain.label: Major modifications left undocumented, unreported to the FAA, and flight testing signed off but not performed
chain.trigger: There are no records that the pilot notified any FSDO of any other major modifications to the airplane... there was no evidence that the airplane had accumulated 3 hours of flight time before the pilot signed off the testing as completed

caused_by.evidence: it was not subject to the more rigorous flight test and analysis that was required to be performed on custom-built airplanes to substantiate the structural loads, flutter characteristics, weight and balance limits, and flight envelope

chain.label: Elevator trim modified to a single controllable left tab, removing redundancy and raising left-tab aerodynamic load
chain.trigger: the use of a single, controllable elevator trim tab (installed on the left elevator) increased the aerodynamic load on the left trim tab (compared to a stock airplane, which has a controllable tab on each elevator)

caused_by.evidence: many structural and flight control modifications that were undocumented and for which no flight testing or analysis had been performed to assess their effects on the airplane's structural strength, performance, or flight characteristics

chain.label: Filler material added to elevator trim tabs increased tab weight and moved tab CG aft
chain.trigger: filler material on the elevator trim tabs (both the controllable left tab and the fixed right tab) increased the potential for flutter because it increased the weight of the tabs and moved their center of gravity aft

caused_by.evidence: modifications... were undocumented and for which no flight testing or analysis had been performed

chain.label: Deteriorated, reused locknut inserts allowed the trim tab attachment screws to work loose
chain.trigger: the fiber locknut insert material applied little to no clamping pressure on the screw threads, and all of the inserts showed evidence of age and reuse

chain.label: Recurrent screw looseness repeatedly retightened instead of replacing the deteriorated hardware
chain.trigger: the screws likely needed to be tightened several times over the course of the airplane's recent racing career, providing the ground crew with an indication of a recurrent problem and opportunities to identify and replace the deteriorated hardware

caused_by.evidence: The loosening of the trim tab attachment screws and the deteriorated condition of the locknut inserts should have been noticeable to the ground crew

chain.label: Reverse-bending fatigue crack grew in the left trim tab inboard hinge attachment screw
chain.trigger: The left trim tab's inboard hinge screw showed evidence of reverse bending fatigue, and corrosion on the fatigue fracture features indicated that the fatigue cracking had been present for a prolonged time

caused_by.evidence: The loose locknut connection allowed for larger load oscillations and the initiation and growth of fatigue cracks
opportunities to identify and replace the deteriorated hardware

chain.label: Pilot raced the airplane at record speeds without any flight testing in the racing regime
chain.trigger: the airplane's maximum 458-knot GPS ground speed between pylons 6 and 7 during the accident flight was the fastest that the airplane had flown on the course by about 35 knots

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's operation of the airplane in the unique air racing environment without adequate flight testing

chain.label: Reduced elevator trim system stiffness allowed aerodynamic flutter of the elevator trim tabs at racing speed
chain.trigger: the reduced stiffness of the elevator trim tab system that allowed aerodynamic flutter to occur at racing speeds

caused_by.evidence: deteriorated locknut inserts that allowed the trim tab attachment screws to become loose

the increasing looseness of the elevator trim tab screws at race speeds and the fatigue crack in one screw resulted in a decrease in the elevator trim system structural stiffness, which was conducive to allowing a flutter event to develop
The addition of filler material to the elevator trim tabs (which increased their weight and moved their CG aft) also increased the potential for flutter
the left trim tab was subject to increased aerodynamic loads (compared to the stock system that uses two moveable trim tabs)
Aircraft speed and structural stiffness are two inputs that govern flutter; as speed increases or structural stiffness decreases, the susceptibility to flutter will increase

chain.label: Left trim tab link assembly buckled and fractured in bending overload, followed by the right tab's fixed link assembly
chain.trigger: Excitation of the flutter resulted in dynamic compressive loads in the left elevator trim tab's link assembly that increased beyond its buckling strength, causing a bending fracture

caused_by.evidence: Flutter would be capable of producing sufficient dynamic loads to buckle and fracture the link assembly

chain.label: Loss of the left tab's downward force caused sudden uncommanded up-elevator deflection and a large aft stick force
chain.trigger: the loss of the left trim tab's downward force on the elevator resulted in a concurrent sudden upward deflection of the elevator, a sudden and forceful aft movement of the control stick

caused_by.evidence: With the link assembly broken, the left elevator trim could no longer provide downward force on the elevator

because of this significant trim input on one tab, the sudden breakage of the left trim tab link assembly... would have significantly increased the force needed for the pilot to hold the control stick in the original position, such that the pilot would have been unable to hold the control stick in position

chain.label: Left roll upset from 73 to 93 degrees of bank, then a right-rolling climb
chain.trigger: the airplane rolled from its established approximate 73-degree-left-bank turn to about 93 degrees left bank, and vertical acceleration reached about 11 G. After the left roll upset, the airplane entered a right-rolling climb maneuver

caused_by.evidence: The sudden application of the aft force would have likely reduced the pilot's ability to precisely hold the right stick input, which resulted in a momentary left roll

chain.label: Rapid pitch-up drove vertical acceleration from about 3 G to 17.3 G in about one second
chain.trigger: within about 1 second, the vertical G levels rose from about 3 G to 17.3 G; both the rate of G onset and the high-G level exceeded human tolerance

caused_by.evidence: a sudden and forceful aft movement of the control stick, the pitch-up of the airplane, and the rapid increase in G
However, during the roll events, the airplane also rapidly pitched up

chain.label: G-induced loss of consciousness; pilot completely incapacitated
chain.trigger: the pilot's time of useful consciousness was likely less than 1 second. As a result, the pilot soon became completely incapacitated

caused_by.evidence: both the rate of G onset and the high-G level exceeded human tolerance... consistent with photographs showing that the pilot was slumped in the cockpit during the climb

chain.label: Uncontrolled helical descent into the airport ramp in the spectator box seating area; airplane fragmented
chain.trigger: collided with the airport ramp in the spectator box seating area following a loss of control... The airplane sustained substantial damage, fragmenting upon collision with the ramp

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's continued climb and helical descent occurred without his control

chain.label: Pilot and 10 people on the ground killed; at least 64 others injured
chain.trigger: The pilot and 10 people on the ground sustained fatal injuries, and at least 64 people on the ground were injured (at least 16 of whom were reported to have sustained serious injuries)

caused_by.evidence: the airplane collided with the airport ramp in the spectator box seating area and scattered wreckage debris in the box seating area, ramp, and grandstands
